manuscript.title: Sacubitril/valsartan versus enalapril for cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of [[k]] randomised trials

abstract._limit: 300 words. Counted at build time and the build fails if exceeded.
abstract.Background: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition changed the treatment of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on the strength of a single large trial. Because that trial dominates the guidelines and every later synthesis, what the accumulated randomised evidence shows when it is not treated as the answer on its own is a different question, and the one this review asks.
abstract.Methods: PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched on [[search_date]] with no language, date or publication-status filter. Randomised trials of sacubitril/valsartan against enalapril in adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction were eligible if they reported the composite of cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure as a time-to-first-event hazard ratio. Hazard ratios were pooled on the log scale by generic inverse variance under a random-effects model with the [[estimator]] estimator. Risk of bias used the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomised trials, effect-of-assignment variant, assessed independently by two assessors. Certainty used the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.
abstract.Results: [[n_records]] records were screened and [[k]] trials contributing [[n_total]] randomised participants met all eligibility conditions. The pooled hazard ratio was [[pooled]] ([[ci_low]] to [[ci_high]]), an interval that includes no effect. Heterogeneity was moderate and estimator-dependent, with I-squared [[i2]] percent under the registered estimator. The pooled result is dominated by one trial: omitting the largest gives [[loo_paradigm]], and each of the three remaining trials has an interval that includes no effect. No risk-of-bias domain was rated high. Certainty was [[certainty]].
abstract.Conclusions: Across [[k]] randomised trials the pooled estimate is compatible with no difference between sacubitril/valsartan and enalapril for a first cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation. The point estimate favours sacubitril/valsartan and rests almost entirely on one large trial; the three smaller trials are individually and jointly compatible with no effect. This is an argument for reading that one trial as the evidence base rather than treating the pooled average as confirmation of it.

introduction.text: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction carries a mortality and rehospitalisation burden that renin-angiotensin system inhibition reduces but does not remove. Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition was developed to act on a second pathway at the same time, combining neprilysin inhibition, which raises natriuretic peptide concentrations, with angiotensin receptor blockade.
introduction.basis: Background framing consistent with the included trials' own rationale sections.

introduction.text: The pivotal comparison against enalapril reported a substantial reduction in the composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation and was stopped early by prespecified rule for overwhelming benefit. That trial is the reason the drug entered guidelines, and it remains by a wide margin the largest randomised comparison of these two agents on this endpoint.
introduction.basis: PARADIGM-HF, cited in the reference list; the early-stopping fact is recorded in inputs.trials[].risk_of_bias.

introduction.text: Three later randomised comparisons against the same active comparator have reported the same composite in different populations. None was powered to detect the effect the pivotal trial found, one reports the composite as a secondary rather than a primary endpoint, and two enrolled a single aetiology. They are nonetheless the only additional randomised evidence on this estimand.
introduction.basis: PARACHUTE-HF and PARALLEL-HF, from inputs.trials[]; endpoint rank from results.per_trial[].endpoint_rank_in_its_own_trial.

introduction.text: A meta-analysis in which one trial contributes most of the information is often criticised as adding nothing to that trial. The criticism is worth taking seriously rather than deflecting, and it is why this review reports leave-one-out as a principal result rather than a sensitivity appendix. The question it can answer is not whether the drug works, which the pivotal trial addresses directly, but how much of the pooled estimate survives that trial's removal.
introduction.basis: Authored rationale for the analysis plan; the leave-one-out result it points to is in results.sensitivity.

methods_prose.heading: Protocol and registration
methods_prose.text: The protocol was registered before any query was executed, as a timestamped commit in a public repository, and is reachable at a SHA-pinned permalink that cannot be rewritten without changing the hash. The interval between registration and the first executed query was [[ordering_margin]], and the ordering is re-tested at every build rather than asserted once. Amendments are recorded as further commits, each marked according to whether it precedes or post-dates the first search, so a reader can see which decisions were made in ignorance of the results and which were not.

methods_prose.heading: Eligibility criteria
methods_prose.text: Trials were eligible if they randomised adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction to sacubitril/valsartan or to enalapril and reported the composite of cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalisation as a time-to-first-event hazard ratio. The fourth condition is a condition on the reported quantity, not on quality. Several excluded records are large, well conducted, and directly concerned with this drug; they are excluded because they report a different estimand, and the supplement records for each one which axis it failed and what it reported instead.

methods_prose.heading: Information sources and search
methods_prose.text: PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched on [[search_date]]. The query strings are reproduced in the supplement exactly as sent, with the endpoint, the parameters, the filters and the UTC time of execution, so that the search can be re-run rather than merely described. No language, date or publication-status filter was applied. [[n_records]] records were returned and every one is listed with its disposition.

methods_prose.heading: Study selection and data collection
methods_prose.text: Records were screened against the eligibility axes, and each exclusion records the axis that failed and, where the failure was on a reported quantity, the quantity the record gave instead. One inclusion decision reversed a screener's original exclusion; that adjudication is shown as an override naming the adjudicator and the time, rather than being absorbed silently into the included set.

methods_prose.heading: Effect measures and synthesis
methods_prose.text: Hazard ratios were analysed on the log scale by generic inverse variance, with the standard error implied by each published interval. A random-effects model was fitted with the [[estimator]] estimator of the between-study variance; DerSimonian-Laird was not used, because it is known to be biased when the number of trials is small, and with [[k]] trials that condition holds. Heterogeneity is reported as tau-squared alongside I-squared, because I-squared is a proportion and says nothing about the magnitude of the between-trial spread. Results were computed with metafor under R at build time; the figures on this page are drawn from the stored estimates, not recomputed in the browser.

methods_prose.heading: Risk of bias
methods_prose.text: Each pooled result was assessed with RoB-2 using the effect-of-assignment variant, at the level of the result being pooled rather than the trial overall. Two assessors worked independently, drawn from different model families and excluding whichever assembled this object. Every signalling question answer is published in the supplement. Agreement is reported as measured, before reconciliation, and disagreements that remain open are shown as open.

methods_prose.heading: Certainty and robustness
methods_prose.text: Certainty was rated with GRADE. Robustness was examined by leave-one-out and by refitting under alternative between-study variance estimators, following the Cochrane Handbook's guidance that sensitivity analysis should test the decisions capable of changing the conclusion. The whole analysis was independently recomputed by a second engine and the two were compared to a stated tolerance.

results_prose.heading: Study selection
results_prose.text: [[n_records]] records were screened and [[k]] trials met all four eligibility conditions, contributing [[n_total]] randomised participants. The count of eligible trials is reported as a LOWER BOUND rather than as a settled number, because a small number of records could not be resolved to a decision from what is publicly reachable; treating an unresolved record as an exclusion would be an assumption presented as a count. The flow of records through screening, with the stages this corpus never recorded stated as such, is shown in the PRISMA figure.

results_prose.heading: Trial characteristics
results_prose.text: The [[k]] trials differ in ways that matter for interpretation. One is a large double-blind trial reporting this composite as its own primary endpoint. Two enrolled chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy, one of them open-label with blinded adjudication and reporting this composite behind a win-ratio primary. One is double-blind and small. Characteristics are in Table 1 and per-arm counts in Table 2. Characteristics of the included trials are given in the table of included studies and their per-arm event counts in the table of per-arm counts.

results_prose.heading: Primary synthesis
results_prose.text: The pooled hazard ratio was [[pooled]] ([[ci_low]] to [[ci_high]], [[ci_level]]% interval), favouring sacubitril/valsartan over enalapril. Between-trial heterogeneity was low: I-squared [[i2]]%, tau-squared [[tau2]], with Q of [[q]] on [[df]] degrees of freedom. The individual estimates range from [[min_point]] to [[max_point]], and that spread is real even though the heterogeneity statistics are small, because three of the four intervals include the null and two of those span more than a doubling of risk. The per-trial and pooled estimates are shown in the forest plot. The prediction interval for a future study runs from [[pi_low]] to [[pi_high]].

results_prose.heading: Robustness
results_prose.text: The pooled result is not robust to the removal of the largest trial. Omitting it gives [[loo_paradigm]], an interval that includes the null. The three smaller trials are therefore individually and jointly compatible with no effect on this composite, and the pooled estimate is best read as the large trial's result, slightly attenuated by the three smaller trials, which neither confirm nor contradict it. Refitting under alternative between-study variance estimators did not change this conclusion. Each refit is shown in the leave-one-out figure and tabulated in the leave-one-out table; [[loo_n_excluding_null]] of [[loo_n_total]] refits still exclude no difference.

results_prose.heading: Cross-engine verification
results_prose.text: The whole synthesis was recomputed independently and the two engines agreed on the point estimate and both bounds to within the stated tolerance, with Q and its degrees of freedom matching exactly. This establishes that the arithmetic is reproducible; it does not establish that the inputs are correct, and it is reported as the former only.

results_prose.heading: Risk of bias
results_prose.text: No domain in any trial was rated at high risk of bias by either assessor. The two assessors agreed on [[rob2_agree]]/[[rob2_total]] domain judgements ([[rob2_rate]]%), and on [[rob2_overall_agree]] of [[rob2_overall_total]] overall judgements. That agreement rate is markedly lower than the agreement observed at screening, and it is published because an unreported agreement rate is not the same as a high one. Per-domain judgements from both assessors are shown in the risk-of-bias figure.

results_prose.heading: Certainty of the evidence
results_prose.text: GRADE certainty for this outcome is [[certainty]], downgraded for risk of bias and for imprecision. The completed RoB-2 assessment was checked against the risk-of-bias downgrade and did not change it, for reasons given in the discussion.

results_prose.heading: Subgroup analysis
results_prose.text: One subgroup analysis was performed and it was NOT pre-specified. Splitting the pool by aetiology gives [[strat1_point]] ([[strat1_low]] to [[strat1_high]]) across the [[strat1_k]] trials in unrestricted heart failure and [[strat2_point]] ([[strat2_low]] to [[strat2_high]]) across the [[strat2_k]] trials restricted to Chagas cardiomyopathy. The test for interaction returns p = [[interaction_p]] and a ratio of hazard ratios of [[rhr]] ([[rhr_low]] to [[rhr_high]]), so the difference between the strata is compatible with chance. Splitting on aetiology does not explain the heterogeneity: the residual I-squared within strata is higher than the overall value, not lower. Because the analysis is post hoc it is reported as hypothesis-generating and is labelled post hoc wherever it appears, in keeping with the Cochrane Handbook v6.5 section 10.11.5 caution against presenting unplanned subgroup contrasts as findings.

results_prose.heading: Small-study effects
results_prose.text: A funnel plot is shown and Egger's regression test was run for completeness, returning an intercept of [[egger_intercept]] with p = [[egger_p]]. Neither is interpreted. At [[k]] trials the Cochrane Handbook v6.5 section 13.3.5.4 advises against interpreting funnel asymmetry or its tests below about ten studies, and the movement of this p value when the fourth trial entered is what a test with almost no power does rather than evidence about publication bias. No claim about small-study effects is made in either direction.

results_prose.heading: Comparison with published syntheses
results_prose.text: One published synthesis on the same comparison had a readable included-study table and was reconciled against this review trial by trial. [[cmp_checked]] checks were applied to it, of which [[cmp_confirmed]] came back clean, [[cmp_errors]] identified an error and [[cmp_absent]] identified a reporting item that is absent. Its included-study list is also the reason this review's k rose during the build: PARALLEL-HF was eligible on every axis of the frozen question, was absent from the brief this object was built from, and was recovered from that list, verified against its own publication and registry record, and pooled. The full reconciliation, the quoted evidence for every check with its location, and the decomposition of where the two reviews differ are given in the section on comparison with published syntheses.

discussion.heading: Principal findings
discussion.text: Across [[k]] randomised trials and [[n_total]] participants, the pooled hazard of a first cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation with sacubitril/valsartan relative to enalapril was [[pooled]] ([[ci_low]] to [[ci_high]]), an interval that includes no difference, with a pooled hazard ratio of [[pooled]] ([[ci_low]] to [[ci_high]]). The more informative finding is not that number but its structure: it is almost entirely the contribution of one trial, and it does not survive that trial's removal.

discussion.heading: Interpreting the estimate
discussion.text: A pooled hazard ratio of [[pooled]] on this composite is a clinically meaningful reduction if it is real, but the interval does not exclude the null: it runs from 0.746 to 1.018. When ANSWER-HF entered, the pool crossed from an interval that excluded no difference to one that does not, and that crossing is reported rather than described as a robustness footnote. In a four-trial synthesis where one trial carries most of the weight -- PARADIGM-HF holds 59% of it -- the interval is doing less work than it appears to in either direction. The honest reading is that the pivotal trial is the evidence, and that this meta-analysis quantifies how little the three subsequent trials change it, rather than adding independent support.

discussion.heading: Heterogeneity
discussion.text: I-squared of [[i2]]% falls in the band conventionally described as low, and tau-squared is [[tau2]]. It would be a mistake to read that as agreement between the trials. I-squared is the proportion of total variability attributable to between-trial differences, and when two of four trials have wide intervals the within-trial variance is large, so the proportion attributable to between-trial variation is small almost by construction. The point estimates range from [[min_point]] to [[max_point]], which spans a clinically important reduction and essentially no effect. The low heterogeneity statistic and the wide spread of point estimates are both true, and reporting the first without the second would mislead.

discussion.heading: The leave-one-out finding
discussion.text: Removing the largest trial moves the pooled estimate to [[loo_paradigm]]. This is the single most important result in the review and it is reported as a principal finding rather than as a sensitivity check, because a synthesis whose conclusion depends on one of its four inputs should say so where a reader cannot miss it. It does not mean the effect is absent: the three remaining trials are small and their intervals are wide, so they are compatible both with the pivotal trial's effect and with none. It means the pooled interval's exclusion of the null should not be read as four trials agreeing.

discussion.heading: Why the risk-of-bias rating did not change
discussion.text: The completed RoB-2 assessment found no domain at high risk in any trial, which might be taken as grounds to remove the GRADE risk-of-bias downgrade. It was not, for a reason worth stating plainly: RoB-2 has no domain for a trial stopped early for benefit. Early stopping is not a randomisation failure, a deviation from intended intervention, missing outcome data, a measurement problem, or selective reporting of a result. The largest trial was stopped early by prespecified rule for overwhelming benefit, and trials stopped early for benefit tend to overstate the effect they were stopped for. A clean RoB-2 therefore cannot discharge that concern, and reading the absence of a high-risk domain as the absence of a problem would mistake the silence of an instrument for evidence.

discussion.heading: Comparison with other evidence
discussion.text: This review reconciles itself against the one published synthesis on this comparison whose included-study table could be read, trial by trial, and reports the checks applied to it with their denominator in the section on comparison with published syntheses. What can be said from within this review is that its estimate is close to the pivotal trial's own published hazard ratio, which follows arithmetically from that trial's weight and is therefore not independent corroboration.

discussion.heading: Strengths
discussion.text: The protocol was registered before the first query with a machine-checkable ordering test. Every screened record is published with its disposition. Both risk-of-bias assessors' full answers are published unreconciled, with the agreement rate as measured. Every number on every surface is projected from one canonical object, so the manuscript, the tables, the figures and the web page cannot disagree with one another. A disagreement between two sources that this review's own extraction missed is published as an unresolved disagreement rather than silently resolved.

limitations: The synthesis rests on [[k]] trials, one of which contributes most of the weight, and the pooled result does not survive its removal. This is stated as a principal finding rather than a caveat.

The count of eligible trials remains a lower bound, but for a different reason than before: the trial that previously made it one has been resolved and included, and two screening records are still undetermined.
Trial-level hazard ratios were taken from publications; no individual-participant data were obtained, so the composite could not be decomposed into its components on a common time axis.

The trials differ in population, in blinding, and in whether this composite was the trial's own primary endpoint. Pooling them assumes they estimate a common quantity, which is a judgement, not an observation.

Risk of bias was assessed by two AI assessors from different model families rather than by two humans. That is the stated release tier for the web surface; it is not the tier a journal submission requires, and the object records the difference rather than eliding it.
Five of fifteen risk-of-bias domain judgements remain unadjudicated. They are carried at the more cautious of the two judgements, provisionally.

A disagreement between the registry and the publication on serious adverse events in one trial is recorded and unresolved. This review's own multi-source extraction did not detect it; a blinded comparator did.
manuscript.conclusions: In adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction, the pooled hazard of a first cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation with sacubitril/valsartan compared with enalapril was [[pooled]] ([[ci_low]] to [[ci_high]]) at [[certainty]] certainty, an interval consistent with no difference. The estimate rests almost entirely on one large trial and does not survive its removal. One trial carries almost all of the information, and the pooled interval includes no difference; three further trials have not resolved it.

secondary_pools._why_these_are_not_the_primary: The registered estimand is a single quantity: cardiovascular death or first heart-failure hospitalisation, whichever comes first, as a time-to-first-event HAZARD RATIO. These three are RISK RATIOS over the whole follow-up, computed from per-arm counts. A risk ratio and a hazard ratio answer different questions, and the protocol fixes the hazard ratio as the measure, so these cannot be promoted into the primary synthesis.
secondary_pools._why_they_must_not_be_added_up: Two of the three are COMPONENTS of the composite. They share the same participants, so reading them alongside the composite counts the same people more than once. The composite counts FIRST events and is not the sum of its components -- on PARADIGM-HF the components exceed it, which is expected. Nothing here is reconstructed by addition.

considered_and_not_pooled.why: A hierarchical win ratio is not convertible to a hazard ratio or a risk ratio. It compares pairs of patients on an ordered hierarchy of events; there is no arithmetic that turns it into this review's estimand without inventing information.
A ratio of change in a biomarker is not an event-time quantity. Excluded on the measure axis at screening, not omitted here.
The estimand is time to FIRST event. A recurrent-event rate ratio counts repeat events and answers a different question; scope_decisions fixes this.
Reported on different instruments and timepoints across the four trials, and not by all three. No common scale, so no pool.

published_comparison._why: Every paper this project ships carries this section. A synthesis that reports only its own result asks a reader to take the field on trust; one that reconciles itself against the published syntheses on the same question, names what they got right as prominently as what they got wrong, and shows the denominator, can be checked. The classes applied below are the classes this review must itself survive. On the night this section was written, this object failed three of them: analysis panels computed at k=3 under a k=4 headline, a title stating a study count its own contents contradicted, and a figure labelled as a diagnostic it was not drawing.

checks.what: Whether their omission of PARACHUTE-HF is an error or a date
checks.detail: Their search closed 15 September 2023. PARACHUTE-HF reported in 2026. Its absence from their review is CORRECT and is not counted against them. A reconciliation that scored this as a miss would be scoring them for not seeing the future.
checks.quote: systematically searched online databases including PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception till September 15, 2023

checks.what: Whether including a retrospective cohort breaches their OWN stated eligibility
checks.detail: It does not. Their pre-specified criteria admit observational designs explicitly, so Pathadka 2020 is inside their own protocol. This object excludes it because THIS question is restricted to randomised evidence, which is a different question and not a fault in theirs. Checked precisely because population-included-against-the-paper's-own-criterion is one of the classes we look for, and here it is clean.
checks.quote: The pre-defined inclusion criteria were observational studies (retrospective cohorts and prospective cohorts) or RCTs comparing sacubitril

checks.what: Whether the influential non-randomised study was tested
checks.detail: It was, and the result is reported in the body rather than buried: removing Pathadka moves all-cause mortality from 0.57 to 0.85 and heterogeneity from 94 per cent to 0. Reporting a sensitivity analysis that overturns your own headline is good practice and is recorded here as such.
checks.quote: We performed sensitivity analysis by removing the study conducted by Pathadka et al. as it was a retrospective study.

checks.what: Absence of a funnel plot or small-study test
checks.detail: None is reported, and at nine studies none is expected: the Cochrane Handbook advises against interpreting these tests below about ten. Their omission is defensible and is NOT counted as a defect. This object applies the same caution to its own Egger's test at k = 4.

checks.what: Whether the Discussion's significance claim matches the primary estimate
checks.detail: The primary all-cause mortality estimate is RR 0.57 with a 95 per cent interval of 0.31 to 1.04. That interval CONTAINS 1, so the comparison is not statistically significant. The Discussion nevertheless states that all three outcomes, all-cause mortality among them, were significantly higher. The statement is true of their RCT-only sensitivity result, 0.85 (0.78 to 0.93), and is not true of the analysis the abstract leads with. It is an error of precision rather than a fabricated number, and it is recorded that way.
checks.quote: The present meta-analysis reported that the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and cardiovascular hospitalization was significantly higher in patients receiving enalapril compared to patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan.

checks.what: Whether the abstract's headline carries the heterogeneity it rests on
checks.detail: The abstract reports RR 0.57 (0.31 to 1.04) for all-cause mortality with no mention that I-squared for that pool is 94 per cent, nor that removing one retrospective study takes it to 0 and moves the estimate to 0.85. A pooled estimate at I-squared 94 is an average over results that disagree, and an abstract is where most readers stop. Their own body text is transparent about both facts; the abstract is not.
checks.quote: Significant heterogeneity was reported among the study results (p = 0.001; I-square: 94%).

checks.detail: No Cochrane RoB, Jadad, Newcastle-Ottawa or equivalent appears anywhere in the text. The JBI reference is to the study-SELECTION protocol, not to an appraisal of the included studies. Risk of bias is a required PRISMA item, and pooling a retrospective cohort with randomised trials is exactly the situation it exists to surface.
checks.quote: The selection and critical appraisal of studies adhered to the Joanna Briggs Institute's (JBI) protocol, which offers a more precise and stringent set of criteria for the study selection process.

checks.detail: PROSPERO is not mentioned and no registration of any kind is stated, so the analysis cannot be checked against a pre-specified plan. Recorded as an absence rather than an error: an unregistered review is not a wrong one. This object states its own registration as a timestamped public commit with an ordering test, so it is a standard we hold ourselves to.

denominator.statement: 13 checks were applied to this review and 9 came back clean. The denominator is stated because a list of only the failures is not a finding, it is a selection.
denominator.symmetry: Confirmations are listed in the same table, in the same detail, as errors. Two checks were designed to catch a fault and instead cleared the paper: including a cohort study is inside their own stated eligibility, and omitting a small-study test at nine studies is what the Handbook advises.

divergence_decomposed.ours: HR 0.872 (0.746 to 1.018) for cardiovascular death or first heart-failure hospitalisation, k=4, time-to-first-event.
divergence_decomposed.theirs: RR 0.76 (0.66 to 0.86) for cardiovascular hospitalisation and RR 0.75 (0.62 to 0.91) for cardiovascular mortality, reported as separate outcomes.
divergence_decomposed.why_they_differ: Four reasons, none of which is an error by either side: a different estimand (hazard of a FIRST event against risk over whole follow-up); a different eligible set (they admit observational designs, we do not); a different search window (ours includes two trials published after theirs closed); and a different composite (they report hospitalisation and cardiovascular death separately, we pool the composite of the two). Decomposed rather than asserting ours is right: on the trials and the quantity the two reviews share, they agree.

INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_2026_08_18.found_by: An INDEPENDENT BLINDED REVIEW run on OpenAI's GPT-5 via Codex, given this object cold with no knowledge of any conclusion reached here.
INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_2026_08_18.what_it_found: The object simultaneously INCLUDED and EXCLUDED ANSWER-HF -- the trial whose presence decides whether the pooled interval crosses 1. results.per_trial included it; screening, scope_decisions and outcomes_considered still recorded the superseded exclusion.
INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_2026_08_18.the_decision_every_field_now_states: ANSWER-HF IS IN THE POOL. k=4. It is flagged HIGH RISK on selection of the reported result, because its contributed endpoint is NOT REGISTERED AT ANY RANK in its own registration. k=3 stands as the SENSITIVITY analysis, not the primary.
INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_2026_08_18.why_this_matters_more_than_a_tidy_up: Omitting ANSWER-HF gives HR 0.8333 (0.7473-0.9292); including it gives 0.8715 (0.7461-1.0181). THE INTERVAL CROSSES 1 ONLY WITH IT IN. A reader who checks this object found it contradicting itself about the single trial that decides the inference.
INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_2026_08_18.nothing_deleted: Every superseded verdict is kept and labelled with its date and reason. The same treatment given to the 852-empty-templates retraction and the projection vocabulary: a record that shows a decision being corrected is worth more than one that was always right.
INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_2026_08_18.the_general_finding: This is the object-page divergence law operating INSIDE A SINGLE OBJECT. Three surfaces had already been found drifting from what they report on -- a commit message from its diff, a batch report from its gate, a page from its object. This is the fourth, and the closest to home.

This is markedly lower than the two-assessor agreement seen at screening, which is what we predicted before running it. Almost no published review reports its RoB-2 inter-assessor agreement at all, so there is no external benchmark. We publish it because an unreported agreement rate is not the same as a high one.

steps.reason: Three separate features, each read from a staged source rather than assumed. PARACHUTE-HF describes itself as an 'open-label, multicenter randomized clinical trial' with blinded endpoint adjudication; blinded adjudication protects how an event is classified but not the unblinded management decisions that produce a heart failure hospitalization, which is one of the two components. In the same trial this composite is the first SECONDARY endpoint, the primary being a win ratio, so the result pooled here comes from that trial's secondary hierarchy and carries the multiplicity and selective-reporting exposure that goes with it; the separate question of the trial not being POWERED for this endpoint is random error and is carried in the imprecision domain, not here. PARADIGM-HF 'was stopped early, according to prespecified rules ... because the boundary for an overwhelming benefit with LCZ696 had been crossed', and a trial stopped early for benefit tends to overstate the effect it was stopped for -- which matters here because the leave-one-out analysis shows the pooled benefit rests on that trial. One level, not two: the trials are randomised, centrally adjudicated and large, and none of the three features is a failure of randomisation.

cvdeath_or_hfh_first.rob2_effect_on_risk_of_bias_rating:
Effect on the GRADE risk-of-bias rating: it does NOT move. It was serious before the assessment and remains serious. Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one.

First, RoB-2 confirmed the substance of the downgrade rather than removing it. Both assessors, independently and from different model families, rated PARACHUTE-HF domain 2 as SOME CONCERNS on the open-label deviations point, which is the first of the three features the rating was already built on. The second assessor also rated its domain 5 as SOME CONCERNS on the selective-reporting point, which is the second feature. The assessment agreed with the reasoning the rating rested on.

Second, and this is why 'no domain reached HIGH' does not discharge the downgrade: RoB-2 has no domain for a trial stopped early for benefit. Early stopping is not a randomization failure, a deviation, missing data, a measurement problem, or selective reporting of a result; it is a stopping-rule effect on the magnitude of the estimate, and the RoB-2 tool does not ask about it in any of its five domains. PARADIGM-HF was stopped early by prespecified rule for overwhelming benefit and the leave-one-out analysis shows the pooled benefit rests on that trial. That third feature is therefore untouched by a clean RoB-2 result, and it alone sustains a serious rating. Reading 'no domain HIGH' as grounds to remove the downgrade would be mistaking the silence of a tool for the absence of a problem.
cvdeath_or_hfh_first.opposite_reading_recorded: The opposite reading is available and is recorded here rather than suppressed: under a common mapping, trials at SOME CONCERNS with none at HIGH support 'not serious', which would raise certainty from low to moderate. We do not adopt it, for the stopping-rule reason above, and because five of fifteen domain judgements are still unadjudicated -- changing a published certainty rating on the strength of a disagreement set nobody has resolved would be the wrong direction to move under uncertainty.
